title: Blood loss after a road accident
body: A 35-year-old man loses a large amount of blood in a road accident. On arrival at the hospital his blood pressure is low. Doctors note that the blood flow and blood pressure in his glomeruli have fallen, and his glomerular filtration rate (GFR) is below normal. His body fluid volume is also reduced. Within a short time, several hormonal feedback mechanisms that involve the hypothalamus, the juxta glomerular apparatus (JGA) and, to some extent, the heart begin to act on his kidneys and blood vessels to bring his blood pressure and GFR back towards normal while he receives treatment.
